summary: Tested the post-submit reset + confirmation alert fix in /app/frontend/app/(app)/submit.tsx. Reset behaviour WORKS on web (form fully cleared after successful submit + tab re-open). However the native Alert.alert popup does NOT render on web (react-native-web@0.21.0 ships Alert.alert as a no-op class — `static alert(){}` in node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js). Consequence: (1) no visible 'Vehicle submitted' pop-up on the web preview; (2) router.replace('/(app)') inside the OK button's onPress is NEVER invoked, so the dealer is NOT redirected home after submit — they stay on the (now-cleared) submit screen. The reset half of the fix is correct; the popup + navigation half is broken on web and needs a cross-platform modal.

ui_bugs.issue: Alert.alert('Vehicle submitted', ...) is a no-op on react-native-web@0.21.0 (see node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js — class Alert { static alert(){} }). On the web preview the confirmation popup NEVER renders, and because router.replace('/(app)') is placed inside the OK button's onPress callback, that navigation ALSO never fires. Verified: after successful submit (FB-000216 was created on backend), URL remained https://.../submit and no browser dialog was captured by Playwright's dialog handler. On native (iOS/Android) Alert.alert would work, but the user's stated bug report ("can a pop up appear saying that vehicle has been submitted") is on web today. Fix: use a cross-platform confirmation Modal (there is already <Modal> imported in submit.tsx for the billing sheet) OR branch on Platform.OS === 'web' with a custom overlay and always fire router.replace('/(app)') after the API call regardless of the alert result.

integration_issues.issue: After the API call succeeds (verified /api/submissions/my returns the new FB-000216 with manual_entry=true, mileage=55000) the app is left sitting on the /submit screen because router.replace lives only inside Alert.alert's OK onPress, which does not fire on web. Dealer has no explicit success signal and no auto-navigation.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: `ImagePicker.MediaTypeOptions` is deprecated — use `ImagePicker.MediaType` (or an array). Fires 5 times per submission on the photo grid. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(app)/submit.tsx lines 728, 755, 772.

Runtime warnings on every submit-screen mount: `"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow"`, `"textShadow*" style props are deprecated`, `Image: style.resizeMode is deprecated — use props.resizeMode`, `props.pointerEvents is deprecated — use style.pointerEvents`. Not blocking but should be swept across theme/components.

action_items: Replace `Alert.alert('Vehicle submitted', ...)` in performSubmit with a cross-platform confirmation. Recommended: reuse the existing <Modal> pattern (like billingConfirmOpen) with a testID='submit-success-modal', an OK button with testID='submit-success-ok', and put router.replace('/(app)') in that button's handler.

As a safety net, ALWAYS call `router.replace('/(app)')` after `resetForm()` regardless of whether the confirmation modal is dismissed — otherwise if the user closes the modal without hitting OK the submit tab stays stuck.
Optionally include the returned submission reference (already extracted as `submittedRef` from resp.submission.reference) inside the modal body so the dealer sees e.g. 'FB-000216 received'.
Migrate `ImagePicker.MediaTypeOptions.Images` → `ImagePicker.MediaType.image` / `['images']` in submit.tsx (3 occurrences) to silence the deprecation warning.
critical_code_review_comments: submit.tsx is now 2450 lines — well past the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting: manual-entry section, photos section, damage/recon section, and the billing/success modals into dedicated components.

performSubmit relies on Alert.alert callback for navigation — even on native this couples the redirect to user interaction. Prefer: navigate first (or use a modal we control), THEN show acknowledgement.
resetForm() intentionally sets vin & engineNo to 'TBC' (line 871) — matches initial state, fine, but worth a code comment that these strings aren't 'empty' from the user's perspective.
seed_data_creation: Created submission FB-000216 (Toyota Corolla 1.8 XS CVT, 2021 reg, 55,000 km, manual_entry=true, unseen=true) for dealer dave@fourbuy.co.za during the flow test. Also reset dave@fourbuy.co.za password to Dave1234! via /api/admin/dealers/{id}/password (was 401 before).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Dave's password had drifted — I reset via admin API to Dave1234!. To repro: login as dave → home → tap Get Cover tile → toggle manual entry + unseen → fill make/fuel/yop/trans/model/deriv/yr-reg → pick colour via wheel picker → fill mileage-input → upload 5 photos through file_chooser on each `photo-<key>` TouchableOpacity → tap submit-button → tick billing-confirm-check → tap billing-confirm-submit. On web the alert is invisible (RN-Web Alert.alert is a no-op class) so no dialog + no navigation, but the form IS reset. Playwright's page.on('dialog') will capture zero dialogs — that alone confirms the popup is missing on web.
rca_of_issue: Root cause: react-native-web ships a stub Alert implementation (class Alert { static alert(){} } — verified in node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js). Calling Alert.alert on the web target executes nothing — no window.alert, no modal, no button callback. E1 placed both the user-facing confirmation AND the router.replace navigation inside that no-op call, so on web the dealer gets zero acknowledgement AND is stranded on the (cleared) submit screen. On native (iOS/Android) the RN core Alert bridges to native UIAlertController / DialogFragment and would work. Mitigation: replace Alert.alert with a cross-platform <Modal>-based success screen, or Platform.select an OS-appropriate implementation; either way move the router.replace OUT of the OK button callback (call it unconditionally after resetForm).
